newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TONGAAT-HULETT PLANS ZIMBABWE SUGAR MILL.
newsitem.headline: TONGAAT-HULETT PLANS ZIMBABWE SUGAR MILL.

text.p: South Africa's Tongaat-Hulett Group Ltd said on Thursday it planned to build a 260 million rand sugar mill in the Lower Mozoe valley, northeast of Harare, in Zimbabwe.
Group managing director Bruce Dunlop said in a statement on Thursday the mill's capacity would be about 140,000 tonnes of sugar a year.

"Cane will be sourced from crop farmers in the Mazoe valley who are looking to diversify into sugar cane production," Dunlop said, adding that provision was also being made for participation by communal growers.
Dunlop said he expected the mill to receive its first cane for crushing in May 1999.
The project is a joint venture between Tongaat-Hulett Sugar, Tate & Lyle Plc and the Lomaz Farmers' Co-operative.
Tongaat-Hulett's share would be held through its wholly owned Zimbabwean subsidiary Triangle Sugar Corporation.
Triangle's equity share in the venture would be provided by plant and equipment from the Mount Edgecombe mill, which was closed two years ago as part of a Tongaat-Hulett rationalisation exercise.
Dunlop said the Zimbabwe sugar industry was well known to the Tongaat-Hulett group through Triangle Sugar Corporation, which expected to produce more than 300,000 tonnes of sugar this year.

"Zimbabwe was selected for expansion in view of its status as one of the world's lowest cost producers of sugar and because growers have already demonstrated their abilities as crop farmers," he said.
Tongaat-Hulett Sugar's technical division would manage the construction contract while operational management would be provided through a joint venture between Tongaat-Hulett Sugar and Tate & Lyle.
The investment complemented the group's southern African sugar strategy which focused on expanding into low cost producing areas.

"Together with expansion plans at Triangle and the Lower Mazoe mill, Tongaat-Hulett will in the medium term be producing over 500,000 tonnes of sugar in Zimbabwe alone, providing significant earnings growth," he said.
